artifactEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI’s September 11 desktop update added a quick chat to the floating Pets controls on macOS and Windows. OpenAI calls that small new chat Quick Chat. The useful part is the small control panel: you can type or speak a new request while another app is open, then use its bell to see whether a chat is running, needs your input, is ready, or is blocked.

The pet is optional animated appearance around that panel. OpenAI says choosing one changes its appearance, not how ChatGPT completes tasks. If you want the floating controls without an animal, choose Mini in Settings > Pets; Mini means the floating controls without a pet.

The status is useful when you have stepped away from the main window: Needs input means the chat needs your answer, approval, or another decision. Ready means it has finished with unread activity. Those labels describe the chat’s progress; the pet is simply the visible companion beside them.

readerValue.reason: Beyond the headline the reader gains the Mini option, the meaning of the status bell, and the project-context boundary that changes where she should start a chat.

explainBack.question: Why doesn't picking a cute pet make ChatGPT's answers any better, and why might a quick chat seem to 'forget' my project files?
explainBack.answer: The pet is only an appearance layer drawn around the floating controls; OpenAI says selecting one changes how the panel looks, not how ChatGPT completes tasks, so the same model does the same work either way. Separately, any chat started from those floating controls begins outside a project, so it never receives the files and instructions saved there — the chat can only use the context the surface that starts it provides.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer must cite the appearance-versus-task-completion distinction (P003) and the floating-controls-outside-a-project boundary (P006), keeping both attributed to OpenAI's documentation.
explainBack.assessment: The article fully supports this causal answer in ordinary language; both links of the chain are explicit and correctly attributed, so explain-back passes.
